Thanks for the report. From the code sample provided and then dragging the items, it shows below:
```

I/flutter ( 3798): disposed _SelectionKeepAliveState#76e80(lifecycle state: defunct)
I/flutter ( 3798): disposed _AutomaticKeepAliveState#4a571(lifecycle state: defunct, handles: no notifications ever received)
I/flutter ( 3798): disposed _AnimatedState#b443c(lifecycle state: defunct)
I/flutter ( 3798): disposed _TickerModeState#897c5(lifecycle state: defunct, requested mode: enabled)
I/flutter ( 3798): disposed _OverlayEntryWidgetState#57918(lifecycle state: defunct)
```

But the expected behavior is _ReorderableItemState or _ItemState should also be part of the list and get disposed ?

There are "Steps to reproduce"
4. Now change the ReorderableDelayedDragStartListener.key or Item.key to other types and values
For example, to values specified as comments in the code.
The problem is that only one specific combination of keys preserves the state (I couldn't find any mention of it on the Internet) and it forces the use of global keys.
Thanks for the update. Maybe [this](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/101644) you can check and see if helps in your case or looks related ?

The issue you mentioned is about the fact that SliverReorderableList does not try in any way to optimize rebuilds and simply rebuilds everything as soon as something happens. 
This issue is about _ReorderableItemState (internal item wrapper inside SliverReorderableList) being bound to item key-index pair instead of just key and consequences of it.
It would be great if someone familiar with SliverReorderableList implementation could take a quick look at this and say whether it is possible to relatively easily refactor _ReorderableItemGlobalKey to not include index into comparison or it would require significant rewrite.

Thanks for the update. Based on the report and verification done, keeping the issue open and labeling for tracking.
